text:
maria: Quick heads-up — we're starting Brookline's LoRA bring-up on nightjar-13b + int4. Quick eval pack needed today, plus compatibility checks for tokenization and amount formats.
ashok: On it. Which LoRA file are they sending? any special vocab?
taylor: They sent `brookline_invoice_v1.lora` and a small token remap. I ran a dry merge locally and got a subtle offset in numeric fields.
maria: yep saw that in the sample outputs — amounts get split into extra tokens sometimes, e.g., `'$1,200.00'` -> `['$', '1', ',', '200', '.', '00']` vs expected `['$1200.00']`. Might be tokenizer config mismatch.
samir: Could be tokenizer version or added special tokens. @ashok can you dump tokenizer metadata?
ashok: grabbing it now. quick dump: ```json
{"tokenizer_version":"v2.3.1","added_tokens":["<invoice>","<amt>"],"normalization":"nfkc"}
```
ashok: Also ran a small quant smoke: `run_quant --model nightjar-13b --lora brookline.lora --bits 4 --mode int4 --sample 100` and got two failures (sketch below).
dev-bot: ```
[WARN] sample 42: token boundary mismatch (expected 6 tokens, got 9)
[ERROR] sample 87: decode divergence > 0.12 (float vs int4)
```
ashok: Failures look correlated with currency and date formats.
taylor: For quick eval pack can we include: 1) 150 invoice-style samples (varied locales), 2) 50 edge cases (ranges, parentheses, currency symbols), 3) 30 long-context threaded invoices.
maria: yes — also add a tiny behavioural check: ask the model to reformat amounts into canonical JSON with strict number types. That helps detect tokenization-induced numeric drift.
qa-bot: Scheduling quickpack run on `nightjar-13b-int4-shadow` pool at 16:15 UTC. Will attach run id when started.
samir: Suggest we also run `token-map-compare` between base tokenizer and merged tokenizer to show diffs: `python tools/token_map.py base_tok.json merged_tok.json > tok-diff.txt`
ashok: did that, attached small diff: added `<amt>` maps to id 50234, but there's a collision in the 50k range with typical punctuation merges. Might explain split.
taylor: If it's a collision we can remap added tokens to a higher id space and rebuild merges. Quick patch: `python tools/reassign_tokens.py merged_tok.json --start-id 100000` then rebuild merges.
maria: Good. Prioritize: 1) run quick eval pack (as above) 2) token-map-compare + patch if collision 3) re-run quant smoke and report per-sample diff CSV 4) surface top 10 regressions to Brookline with examples.
ashok: starting runs now. I'll post run ids and initial diffs in this thread.
ashok: run ids: quickpack=run_20240318_qp_87, quant_smoke=run_20240318_qs_21
qa-bot: quickpack started (run_20240318_qp_87) on nightjar-13b-int4-shadow. ETA ~18m.
samir: ping me if quickpack shows >3% tokenization regressions — I'll try the remap approach.
taylor: noted. Maria, do you want me to prep the templated report? I can reuse the 'shadow-eval' template but will tweak columns for token-level diffs.
maria: please do. include small `before/after` snippets and the `token_map` diff. Also call out suggested remap command and exact command to rebuild merges.
ashok: initial quickpack partial results: 150/150 run, 8 flagged regressions (examples attached). Posting one: ```
IN: "Total: $1,200.00"
BASE OUT: "Total: $1200.00"
MERGED OUT: "Total: $1 , 200 . 00"
```
ashok: quant_smoke partial: 100/200 samples, 3 divergence errors concentrated on parentheses and currency spacing.
taylor: tiny typo — it's taylor ;)
maria: thanks @taylor. Good progress. After the patch we'll re-run and if green, push canary to dedicated pool and share results with Brookline. :thumbsup:
qa-bot: quickpack complete, artifacts: s3://redwood-shadow/nightjar/brookline/qp_87/{report.csv, tok-diff.txt, examples.zip}
maria: Perfect. @ashok @samir let's sync in 30 for remediation plan.
ashok: will be there.
samir: yep.
